verificationSummary: Editor commit 5cdd092265eb036be56a2d8f06e3987d0b6199d6 provides an accepted bounded browser-app live Backend corpus smoke for the default loopback Backend corpus. The npm script evidence:editor-browser-live-backend-corpus-smoke starts a live loopback Backend server in process, seeds it with the four default Backend documents backed by Core fixtures, starts the rendered Editor app with VITE_FLOWDOC_BACKEND_URL, launches headless Chrome through CDP, opens /documents, and visits /documents/reorder-blocked-target-qa/design, /documents/product-report-vnext-baseline/design, /documents/product-report-vnext/design, and /documents/product-report-vnext-minimal/design. Retained evidence records the library page exposing exactly those four documents as Migration required with revisions 3, 1, 3, and 3; each design route loads as compatible active API state; clicking Upgrade through the browser UI migrates each document to partial mode and advances revisions to 4, 2, 4, and 4. Backend request evidence includes /documents?limit=24, /capabilities/versions, each document read route, and each /migrations/package-v3-document-v4 route with 200 or 204 statuses. TDD RED failed before implementation because the retained fixture was absent; focused retained evidence then passed. Editor worktree and merged main both ran the write-off evidence script successfully, focused retained evidence test passed, and npm run check passed type-check, 80 test files, 286 tests, and build. Backend and Core were clean and unchanged. This supports only bounded local loopback headless Chrome coverage for the default Backend corpus read/design/migration path; it does not promote FlowDoc or product readiness truth, non-default or broad production corpus coverage, deployed Backend compatibility, cross-browser readiness, accessibility, visual regression, npm audit remediation, or bundle-size readiness.
